newsitem.title: UK: Shell Nigeria Forcados output still down.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria Forcados output still down.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell's Nigerian Forcados crude oil output remains 95,000 barrels a day (bpd) below normal because of continued ethnic clashes in the oil-producing Niger delta swamplands, a Shell official in Lagos said on Monday.
"Production could stay down for some time," the official said.
Shell said on Friday it had declared force majeure on 20 percent of Forcados blend output causing delays of two to three days from April 29 to May 20.
Forcados output in May was expected to run at 475,000 bpd.
No cargo cancellations have yet been announced.
A Shell spokesman on Friday said the number of Shell staff in the troubled area west of the Niger delta had also been reduced.
Renewed clashes in the oil-producing swamps between militant youths of Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes over the relocation of a local council headquarters have claimed many lives.

At the height of the crisis in March, armed Ijaw tribesmen occupied six oil flow stations of the Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group, shutting off 100,000 barrels per day of its crude oil production.
Some 127 of Shell's Nigerian staff held by the tribesmen were released after negotiations and oil production resumed.
At the root of the crisis is a long-standing rivalry among three tribes -- the Ijaws, the Itsekiris and the Urhobos.
